messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: continuous-batching p99 spike in region us-west-2 for model redwood-7b-ql-std. p99 > 2s for 6m. Paging @alex and @jordan. rule: contbatch-p99-usw2

alex: Oncall ack, joining. Any evidence of 5xx or client retries?

maria: No 5xxs. Telemetry: p95 jumped 130ms -> 480ms, p99 ~2.4s. Streaming endpoints showing chunk gaps (clients report stalls ~1.5s between events). Only affects requests routed to cont-batch path.

jordan: Traces show stalls coincident with KV lookups and big padding events. Typical request mix: median seq ~45 tokens but a fat tail ~700-1200 tokens. Scheduler is packing small + huge seq together, causing padding amplification and head-of-line stalls.

alex: Immediate mitigations brainstorm: A) enable seq-bucket isolation in scheduler B) reduce max_batch_size on impacted pool C) flip feature-flag to route cont-batch requests to streaming path (costly). Which to try now?

tess: Ops runbook options: `ops scheduler config apply --pool usw2-contbatch-3 --set max_batch=32 --seq-buckets 0:128,129:512,513:+ --fairness strict` (propagates ~45s). Or `ops feature toggle contbatch redwood-7b-ql-std off` (propagates ~30s).

samir: Quick safe step: try smaller batches + strict per-bucket fairness. Less risky than full flip. I'll prepare a canary change to one node group.

maria: Canary applied to pool nodegroup A -> results within 90s: p95 down to 260ms, p99 down to 1.05s, stall-count down 80%. Replay script: `scripts/replay_mixedseq_load --pool usw2-canaryA --trace sample_longtail.json`

jordan: Good. Note tradeoff: throughput drop ~8% observed in canary due to smaller batch utilization. But customer-visible latency improved.

alex: Execute two-step immediate plan: 1) roll seq-bucket + max_batch=32 to full impacted pool `usw2-contbatch-3`; 2) monitor for 10m, if p99 > 1.5s over any 5m window then flip cont-batch off for the model. Maria, Tess, Samir execute step 1.

ops-bot: Applying `scheduler config` to pool `usw2-contbatch-3` now. Change id: cfg-2026-1795567-1.

maria: Change pushed. Observability: after ~60s p95=290ms, p99=920ms on impacted hosts. Streaming stall rate down from ~22/min to ~4/min.

alex: Monitoring. Start drafting support notifications for customers with >1s p99 exposure (use alert metadata).

support-bot: Pulling alert metadata... matched customers: CustB-chat-prod (high exposure), CustA-embed-batch (medium), CustX-internal (low). Generating support tickets.

jordan: Found KV eviction spikes correlated with token boundary events in goroutine dumps. Example log snippet:
```
kv_cache.go:432 evictCandidate start id=0x7fffa  latency_ms=12
kv_cache.go:459 fetchKV return size=12kb latency_ms=1120
stream_handler.go:218 sendChunk idle_gap_ms=1488
```
This suggests synchronous KV read delays can stall streamer pipeline when long requests finish and trigger large lookups.

samir: Short-term we can stagger KV GC and increase KV read concurrency on these nodes. I'll open a change: `ops nodeset update --pool usw2-contbatch-3 --kv-concurrency 16` to test.

tess: Support message for CustB drafted: "We observed elevated streaming latencies affecting live chat; we've applied scheduling changes to prioritize like-sized sequences and reduced max batch size. We're monitoring; expected stabilization within 30-45 minutes. If we need to switch to streaming-only path we'll notify with runtime/cost implications." Want to add a link to incident page?

alex: Yes include incident page and ETA. ETA: 30-45m for stabilization; will escalate sooner if regressions.

ops-bot: Incident record created: /incidents/2026-03-15-1795567000-contbatch-seqlen-latency. Severity: S2.

maria: Canary -> full roll applied. After 5m p95=310ms, p99=1.0s across pool. Stalls minimal.

alex: OK holding plan: keep cont-batch on with seq-buckets + max_batch=32. Escalate plan B (full flip) if p99 > 1.5s for 3 consecutive 5m windows. I've documented runbook steps: `runbook/contbatch_disable.md` and `playbooks/notify_support.md`. Ticket INF-8921 created to track follow-ups (scheduler heuristics, KV GC, route-by-length).

jordan: I'll investigate KV GC and GC scheduling across replicas — hypothesis: synchronous eviction blocking I/O thread. If true, we should stagger GC windows and add async prefetch for large-KV reads.

samir: I'll work on a longer-term scheduler improvement: dynamic batch caps based on observed seq distribution per window, plus preemptive pack-shed for >512 token requests. Add perf test in harness.

tess: Handoff to night: @jordan will be primary after 22:00 UTC, @alex will be reachable for escalation. Leaving notes in PagerDuty and #customer-impact.

alex: Handoff summary: changes applied: seq buckets [0-128,129-512,513+], max_batch_size=32, kv_concurrency increased on pool. Current metrics: p95 ~300ms, p99 ~1.0s, stall events down ~85%. Support notified for CustB/CustA. Follow-ups: INF-8921 (scheduler), INF-8922 (kv-gc), postmortem scheduled.

jordan: I'll investigate KV GC and GC scheduling across replicas — hypothesis: synchronous eviction blocking I/O thread. If true, we should stagger GC windows and add async prefetch for large-KV reads.

samir: I'll work on a longer-term scheduler improvement: dynamic batch caps based on observed seq distribution per window, plus preemptive pack-shed for >512 token requests. Add perf test in harness.

tess: Handoff to night: @jordan will be primary after 22:00 UTC, @alex will be reachable for escalation. Leaving notes in PagerDuty and #customer-impact.

alex: Handoff summary: changes applied: seq buckets [0-128,129-512,513+], max_batch_size=32, kv_concurrency increased on pool. Current metrics: p95 ~300ms, p99 ~1.0s, stall events down ~85%. Support notified for CustB/CustA. Follow-ups: INF-8921 (scheduler), INF-8922 (kv-gc), postmortem scheduled.

support-bot: Tickets opened: #SUP-1142 (CustB), #SUP-1143 (CustA). Messages sent.

maria: Uploaded trace bundle for postmortem: s3://redwood-ops/contbatch/1795567000/traces.tar.gz. Includes sample trace with padding blowup.

jordan: Oncall ack, will monitor dashboards for 3 hours and be ready to flip feature flag if needed. Also adding a quick alert: `if p99_contbatch_usw2 > 1.5s for 3 windows -> page oncall`: done.

alex: Closing active page. Reopen if any threshold trip. Thanks team for rapid mobilization.

maria: Quick note for PM/engineering: propose default scheduler preset for models with >1% >512 token requests to use seq-bucketed mode and smaller batch caps. Will add to roadmap.

jordan: +1. End thread."
